about.title: Visalia Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Work in Visalia happens on job sites, in warehouses, behind the wheel, and behind a desk, and injuries follow all of those settings. Under California law, workers' compensation is usually your only claim against the employer itself, and it applies no matter who was at fault. That part is fairly settled. What many Tulare County workers miss is the second layer: when someone outside the company caused the harm, a separate injury claim may exist alongside comp. Think of a subcontractor who left a hazard, a property owner who ignored a defect, a manufacturer whose equipment failed, or a driver who hit you while you were on a work errand. Visalia recorded 411 injury collisions in 2025, with 558 people injured and 8 deaths, and public records show the heaviest volumes along Rt 63, S Demaree Street, SR-198, and S Mooney Boulevard. Some of those crashes involved people simply doing their jobs. LawProactive is a free service, not a law firm. We connect you with an independent attorney who works on contingency, so there is no fee unless you recover.

whyChoose.title: Why Visalia Workers Reach Out to LawProactive

items.title: We look past the comp claim
items.desc: Workers' comp is usually the exclusive remedy against your employer, but it is not always the whole story. The attorneys we connect you with check whether a negligent third party, such as a subcontractor, equipment maker, or another driver, opens a separate claim.

items.title: Deadlines get explained early
items.desc: You should report a job injury to your employer within 30 days, and a third-party injury claim carries a two-year deadline in California. An early conversation keeps both clocks in view.

items.title: Retaliation is illegal, and you should know that
items.desc: California law prohibits employers from punishing you for reporting an injury or filing a claim. If you are worried about your job in Visalia, an independent attorney can walk you through your protections before you decide anything.

items.question: I was hit on S Mooney Boulevard while making a delivery for work. Is that just a comp claim?
items.answer: Not necessarily. Because you were working, workers' compensation likely covers your medical care and part of your lost wages regardless of fault. If another driver caused the crash, you may also have a separate injury claim against that driver, which is handled outside the comp system and carries a two-year deadline. An attorney can evaluate both paths together.

items.question: Can my Visalia employer fire me for reporting an injury?
items.answer: No. Retaliation for reporting a work injury or filing a workers' comp claim is illegal in California. You should still report the injury to your employer within 30 days to protect your comp rights. If you have already faced pushback, mention it when you connect with an attorney.

items.question: Does LawProactive charge anything to connect me with a lawyer?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free connection service, not a law firm. The independent attorneys in our network work on contingency, which means there is no fee unless there is a recovery in your case. You are under no obligation after the first conversation.
